title: Lead, Cost Modeling Scientist - Medicines for All
description:
Job Summary

Medicines for All (M4ALL), a part of Virginia Commonwealth
University, is an entrepreneurial, impact-oriented institute
dedicated to dramatically improving global access to lifesaving
medicines. We achieve this through synthetic process innovation and
advanced technology deployment to reduce costs and waste in small
molecule drug substance manufacturing. Our work supports treatments
for diseases such as TB, malaria, HIV, oncology, metabolic
diseases, CNS, and immunology.

As a Lead, Cost Modeling Scientist, you will work within an
experienced team in a fast‑paced environment and contribute to
leading‑edge research and analyses. Under the direction of the
Director of Process Economics and Market Intelligence, this role
handles the following key responsibilities in alignment with
M4ALL’s technical and economic objectives:

Techno‑Economic Modeling

Prepare material balances, chemical raw material cost
estimates, and green chemistry metrics for baseline and proposed
API manufacturing routes.
Drive continuous improvement of cost‑modeling tools and
frameworks to enhance efficiency, transparency, and usability
across the Institute.
Evaluate alternative synthetic routes and provide strategic
recommendations to project teams and leadership on cost saving
opportunities and risk tradeoffs.
Ensure all technoeconomic analyses meet or exceed expectations
for technical quality, reliability, and timeliness, and proactively
identify risks to deliverables.

Data Management & Analysis

Manage the development, accuracy, and governance of raw
material databases, ensuring data integrity, traceability, and
alignment with modeling needs.
Establish standards and best practices for data management
within the Process Economics function.
Lead complex or high‑impact analyses and guide the team in
generating actionable insights for strategic and operational
decision‑making.
Partner with internal stakeholders to anticipate data needs and
ensure analytical readiness for emerging priorities.

Collaboration & Project Support

Serve as an advisor to project teams, providing strategic input
on process changes, development decisions, and cost implications
across the lifecycle of each drug target.
Facilitate alignment between technical teams and leadership by
translating economic findings into clear, decision‑ready
recommendations for both technical and non‑technical
audiences.
Represent the Process Economics function in cross‑functional
discussions, ensuring economic considerations are integrated early
and consistently.
Provide guidance, mentorship, and informal leadership to junior
analysts and researchers supporting techno‑economic work.

Continuous Improvement

Lead the development and refinement of internal tools,
templates, and methodologies that strengthen the institute’s
techno‑economic capabilities.
Identify and implement opportunities to streamline workflows,
improve data quality, and enhance the overall efficiency of the
Process Economics function.
Ensure all work complies with federal, state, and local
regulations, and proactively monitor emerging regulatory or market
trends that may impact economic modeling.

Qualifications:

Required Qualifications

Education: Ph.D. or Master’s degree in Chemistry,
Chemical Engineering, Computational Chemistry, Data Science,
Biology, or a closely related field

Candidates with a Bachelor’s degree and 4–5+ years of
progressively responsible experience in process economics, chemical
process development, or related areas will also be considered.
Candidates with a combination of education and substantial
amount of progressive, relevant experience will also be
considered.


Strong foundational knowledge of Organic chemistry and the
ability to evaluate synthetic routes from both a technical and
economic perspective.
Demonstrated experience leading or overseeing techno‑economic
evaluations, including the ability to assess multiple chemical
processes and guide teams toward cost‑effective, scalable
options.
Ability to do process mapping, unit operation and cycle time of
chemical processes.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and related analytical tools,
with the ability to design, audit, and improve complex cost models
involving material, labor, equipment, and process‑level
assumptions.
Exceptional written communication skills, with experience
preparing decision‑ready reports and recommendations for technical
teams and leadership.
High proficiency with spreadsheets (Excel, Google Sheets,
Smartsheet), ChemDraw, MS Office, and Google Drive, with the
ability to guide others in best practices. Previous experience with
techno economic analysis or chemical route analysis is a plus but
not required.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the
ability to convey information clearly to diverse audiences.
Excellent analytical, problem‑solving, and reasoning abilities,
with the capacity to work under pressure and meet tight
deadlines.
Demonstrated ability to work in and foster an environment of
respect, professionalism and civility with a population of faculty,
staff, and students from all backgrounds and experiences, or a
commitment to do so as a staff member at VCU.
Highly motivated, self‑directed, innovative, and able to work
independently.
Ability to manage and analyze large datasets with accuracy and
attention to detail.
Strong collaboration skills and the ability to work effectively
with researchers and cross‑functional teams, while demonstrating
behaviors aligned with M4ALL’s core values and organizational
culture.
Demonstrated ability to learn new concepts quickly and adapt to
evolving project needs.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in pharmaceutical manufacturing and process
development of active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs).
Experience in chemical process development, route scouting, and
scale-up is preferred.
Experience with data analysis tools (e.g., Python, R,
Scikit-learn, PyTorch, etc.) is a plus.

Additional Details

Salary Range: The annual salary for this position is up to
$125,000, with the final compensation determined based on the
selected candidate’s unique qualifications, experience, and
skills.

Benefits : All full-time university staff are eligible for
VCU’s robust benefits
package that includes comprehensive health benefits, paid annual
and holiday leave, generous tuition benefits, retirement planning
and savings options, tax-deferred annuity and cash match programs,
employee discounts, well-being resources, abundant opportunities
for career development and advancement, and more.

Reporting Structure: This role reports to the Director of
Process Economics & Market Intelligence and embodies everyday
leadership, with an expectation to lead through actions,
discussions, decisions, and interactions. As a role model within
the organization, you will influence others by consistently
demonstrating the values and behaviors that drive our mission
forward.

Work Environment: Upon hire, the workstation will be located
at the VA Bio+Tech Park and may occasionally require travel within
the greater Richmond area. Since M4ALL's inception in 2017, we have
received significant financial support from a diverse portfolio of
major donors. This position is grant-funded, with continued
employment contingent upon ongoing funding.

FLSA Exemption Status: Exempt

Hours per Week: Minimum of 40 hours/week; Monday - Friday
(day shift)

Restricted Position: Yes, continued employment is contingent
upon funding

ORP Eligible: Yes

Flexible Work Arrangement: Yes - This role is hybrid, with
the expectation of being fully onsite during the initial training
period to ensure a strong foundation and smooth onboarding. Hybrid
flexibility will be available once core competencies are met and
the employee is working independently.

University Job Title: Scientist, RS - OPEN

Eligible for sponsorship (e.g. H-IB visa status, etc.): No,
applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without
the need for current or future visa or permanent residence
sponsorship. Sponsorship is not available for this position.

Contact: m4all@vcu.edu
